parameter: how a washed-out delivery is corrected
value: lineart-preserving recolour: detect the render's linework, label the fills it encloses, classify each by median colour and height, repaint from tv639u's measured per-material palette
reason: repin leaves value alone by design, so a washed-out black stays washed out, and no tone curve recovers it either - the failing renders put 51.5 percent of the figure in one midtone block and 25.6 percent at pure white, and a flat white fill has no gradation to open (a highlight curve from p 1.0 to 3.0 moved value>=230 by one point). The refine pass is what bleaches: s53prb went from 38.5 percent dark at generation to 6.3 after the 2048 redraw at denoise 0.55, while xjpwjb held at 40.5, so the loss is per-render and cannot be dialled out. Asserting the colour instead of sampling it removes both the seed lottery and the refine loss: seven deliveries land at 34 to 50 percent dark against the reference's 46.9

parameter: how legwear is told from the dress
value: a fill below RECOLOR_LEG_CY covering at least RECOLOR_LEG_MIN_AREA of the figure is legwear whatever its value
reason: value alone was the first rule and it fails on the renders that most need correcting: rzuioj drew the legs at value 239 and 255, brighter than the dress, so they classified as dress and shipped lavender with the figure at value 173. Size and height separate them cleanly - the leg masses run from 8 percent of the figure upward while the hands and stray hair that also fall that low stay under 2. The rule fixed rzuioj (dress 39.0 to tights 31.5 percent, dark 23.4 to 54.8) and left xl0pgl, which value already classified correctly, unchanged

parameter: how much of a region's own colour survives the repaint
value: hue and saturation keep 0.7 of the region's deviation around the target, bounded to RECOLOR_H_SPREAD either side and RECOLOR_S_CEILING above
reason: pinning each region to one hue and one saturation flattened the drawing and the human called it worse than the uncorrected render: the hair's purple strokes and the blush went with it, and the hair, the face and the dress came out one grey mass with no edge between them - this render carries its shading in hue and saturation, not in value, which the first version assumed. Keeping the deviation unbounded brings back the magenta strokes the render draws over the hands and the face at saturation 174, and keeping their hue deviation turns them teal rather than skin, so the band is what makes both work at once

parameter: which renders the recolour is for
value: washed-out renders only; a healthy render keeps repin
reason: xl0pgl was never washed out - its delivery already sat at 45.4 percent dark against the reference's 46.9 - so the recolour had nothing to win there and only the flattening to lose. The renders it does win on are the ones whose blacks are gone, where no correction of hue or saturation reaches the problem. Left opt-in behind --recolor for that reason rather than made the default
